items.title: Focused Echo for PE in Patients With Abnormal Vital Signs
items.summary: The paper that tells you what a normal-looking heart actually buys you when the patient in front of you is tachycardic and you are deciding whether to chase a PE.
items.note: Daley's multicentre cohort found focused cardiac ultrasound was 92% sensitive for PE across patients with abnormal vitals, and 100% sensitive in the subgroup with a heart rate at or above 110 — but only around 63% specific, so it narrows rather than rules out. This is squarely CCPU basic echo territory: RV strain, probe in hand, before the CTPA is booked. Ultrasound GEL has not appeared in this feed before, and it reviews the POCUS literature study by study, which is the format that actually sticks.

items.title: Journal Feed Weekly Wrap-Up: Torsion, Febrile Infants, IPA
items.summary: Five fresh papers condensed to the one line each that would change a shift, including manual detorsion restoring testicular flow 105 minutes earlier than waiting for theatre.
items.note: The torsion finding is the one with teeth — paediatric EM physicians detorsing at the bedside beat going straight to surgery by nearly two hours of ischaemic time, which is an argument for doing it yourself rather than phoning. Also in here: febrile infants under 90 days without a detectable respiratory virus carry a higher invasive bacterial infection rate than those with one, and an evidence review backing inhaled isopropyl alcohol for acute nausea, unstudied in pregnancy. emDocs carries the JournalFeed wrap-up weekly and none have run in this feed yet.

items.title: Care in Custody: Patients Brought to the ED by Police
items.summary: The handover nobody teaches you: who consents, who can refuse, and who the patient actually belongs to when police bring them through the ambulance doors.
items.note: Every registrar has had the patient in handcuffs with an officer standing at the curtain, and the awkwardness is rarely clinical — it is about capacity, privacy and who is allowed to say no. Brown's residency blog writes at exactly the right altitude for this, practical rather than medicolegal abstraction. A source that has never appeared here, worth keeping for the topics the big FOAM sites skip.

items.title: Ebola outbreak kills more than 5,300 people in DR Congo
items.summary: The Bundibugyo outbreak this feed has been tracking since the first Kenyan case has now passed 10,000 confirmed cases and 5,300 deaths.
items.note: Six weeks ago the WHO notices in this feed were counting contacts released from quarantine in Kenya one by one; the arithmetic has changed scale. From today, passengers flying into the United States must attest they have not been in the DRC in the preceding 21 days, which is the kind of measure that eventually arrives as a screening question at triage. Africa CDC's count is running ahead of WHO's, so expect the official figure to climb.

items.title: Virus outbreaks show urgent need for pandemic treaty, says WHO
items.summary: Tedros uses Ebola and the hantavirus cluster as the argument for finishing the pandemic agreement, which is the governance layer behind every outbreak notice in this feed.
items.note: The treaty is the thing that decides whether the next outbreak's vaccines and diagnostics reach the countries with the cases, and Croakey has already run the Victorian angle on defending it. Worth reading as the system-level counterpart to the DRC case counts rather than as a separate story. Euronews is new here and carries WHO press conferences without a paywall.

items.title: Karate Boogaloo: Some Rules Are Carrots, Some Are Sticks
items.summary: A long Q&A with the Melbourne instrumental soul band about how they actually make a record, from a writer rather than a press release.
items.note: Access All Areas already came through this feed as a Bandcamp link; this is the band explaining the self-imposed constraints behind it, which is the part a release announcement never carries. Karate Boogaloo sit on the College of Knowledge and Colemine side of the same shelf as the Daptone and Big Crown records in the collection, and they do it from Melbourne. Rhythm Passport is a new name here and the interview format is closer to what Owen Cuts did for records writing than any reissue roundup.

items.title: Lomo MC-A Review: The Standard for New Film Cameras
items.summary: A properly new 35mm compact, built rather than reissued, reviewed on how it handles instead of on its spec sheet.
items.note: Compact film cameras have been a secondhand market for twenty years — Kosmo Foto's piece on them returning from the dead ran in this feed in March — and the MC-A is the first one that makes the comparison with a premium point-and-shoot a real argument rather than nostalgia. The review is on build, metering and the autofocus, which is the only way camera writing earns its place here. Reviewers elsewhere flag the loud focus motor and a finicky advance lever, so read it next to that.

items.title: Unboxing 9 Cameras from Buyee
items.summary: What actually arrives when you buy nine cheap film cameras sight-unseen through a Japanese proxy service, condition claims and all.
items.note: Buying from Yahoo Japan through a proxy is how most of the interesting cameras reach Australia now, and the gap between a listing's description and what lands on the bench is the part nobody writes down. Eckman has been reviewing cameras for over a decade, one body at a time, with a scoring system he actually sticks to. Entirely new to this feed and a deeper well than the sites that have been carrying it — worth adding to the source list if he holds up.

items.title: The History of Blanket Coats
items.summary: Where the capote came from, why it was cut from trade blankets, and how the point blanket became a coat you can still buy.
items.note: This is the provenance behind the Pendleton and Woolrich end of the reference points — French sailors trading coats on the Atlantic coast in the 1600s, then Hudson's Bay point blankets turned into full-length garments once the climate demanded it. Heddels' own wool blanket piece is already in the feed and this is the garment half of the same story. Useful now that the weather is turning the other way and the heavy stuff goes back in the wardrobe.

items.title: Coming Soon: Silver Linings, a Wine and Vinyl Bar in Collingwood
items.summary: Natural wine, hibachi cooking and a record-led room on Smith Street from the pair behind 98 Lygon.
items.note: Ben Clark and Simon Aukett's 98 Lygon first look came through this feed last week, so this is the same hands going again at 406 Smith Street — this time with a vinyl rig through vintage Wharfedales and Brian MacAlister on a hibachi. A wine bar where the records are load-bearing is the rare overlap between the two things in this feed that never usually meet. Late spring opening, no firm date yet, so worth knowing before it is booked out.

items.title: 18 New Restaurants, Bars and Cafes to Try This November
items.summary: November's openings, with Tommy Two Buns relocating into Bar Gloria in Fitzroy North after leaving the bowlo.
items.note: The northside entry is the one that matters here — Tommy Two Buns has moved out of the Fitzroy bowling club and into Bar Gloria, which puts it walking distance from the Pinnacle and Champagne Video, both already in this feed. The rest of the month skews west and east, to Yarraville and Camberwell, so this is thinner northside than October was. Read it as a map of where the month went rather than a hit list.

items.title: Games Coming Out In November 2026 You Should Be Excited For
items.summary: The Australian release calendar for the month GTA 6 finally lands, with local dates and platforms rather than American ones.
items.note: GTA 6 is 16 days out on PS5 at $79.99 standard, with preloads reported to open on the 12th, and this feed has been tracking it since the file-size story and the launch trailer. Around it the month carries Zero Parades on the 3rd and The Binding of Isaac: Repentance+ landing the same day as Rockstar, which is a scheduling decision somebody will regret. Press Start is Australian and new here, which matters for release timing in a way the US sites never get right.
